systems.description: North and east arms of the periphery wall at the corner

main_system_reason: The periphery wall is the only long Harappan line on the published plan; the brick walls inside it in trenches Do10-Do11 follow its two arms.
notes: We measured the one plan of the Gola Dhoro (Bagasra) periphery wall in Indian Archaeology - A Review 1996-97 (Fig. 1). It shows the north-east corner of the wall across a grid of trenches. The north and east arms are square to each other within about one and a half degrees, and both are turned about ten degrees anticlockwise from the plan's cardinal directions. The east arm is exposed in four trenches along about 23 m and was fitted as one line. The north star is a small symbol about 32 px tall, which dominates the error; it is drawn parallel to the 5 m trench grid, so the plan's north is in effect the grid's north. The site coordinates given are those of the modern town of Bagasra and are approximate.
